raw.details:
Overview

The Last Daemon — Capture The Flag (CTF) by Beunwrapd

Join the Official WhatsApp Community:
https://chat.whatsapp.com/EpDiRs3oQ1t6riNwVgGJqF

About the Competition

The digital world is full of secrets, vulnerabilities, and hidden information. Are you ready to uncover them?

The Last Daemon is a cybersecurity Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by Beunwrapd, designed to challenge aspiring ethical hackers, cybersecurity enthusiasts, and students through hands-on security problems.

Participants will test their technical knowledge, analytical thinking, investigative abilities, and problem-solving skills across multiple cybersecurity domains. From decoding cryptographic messages to investigating digital evidence and uncovering web vulnerabilities, every challenge will push participants to think critically and approach problems creatively.

Whether you are an experienced CTF player or a beginner exploring cybersecurity, The Last Daemon invites you to test your skills and compete against other participants.

No teams. No shortcuts. Just you, your skills, and the challenge.

Competition Domains

Participants can expect challenges across the following cybersecurity domains:

  • Web Security: Identify vulnerabilities and solve web-based security challenges.
  • Cryptography: Decode encrypted messages and uncover hidden flags.
  • Digital Forensics: Investigate files, metadata, and digital evidence.
  • OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Analyze publicly available information to uncover clues.
  • Reverse Engineering: Analyze programs and uncover their underlying logic.
  • Miscellaneous: Solve unconventional technical puzzles requiring creativity and logical reasoning.

Challenges may vary in difficulty, allowing participants to demonstrate their skills and learn through practical problem-solving.

Eligibility and Participation Guidelines

  • The competition is open to students and cybersecurity enthusiasts interested in ethical hacking and information security.
  • Participants from all colleges, universities, academic disciplines, and specializations are welcome.
  • Participation Mode: Solo Only. Every participant must compete individually.
  • Team formation and team registrations are not permitted.
  • Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are not applicable because this is an individual competition.
  • Every participant must register individually through the official Unstop listing.
  • Participants must use their own registered accounts to access challenges and submit flags.
  • Beginners are welcome. A basic understanding of computers and cybersecurity concepts may be helpful.

Competition Format

  • Competition Type: Capture The Flag (CTF)
  • Participation Mode: Individual / Solo
  • Format: Challenge-based cybersecurity competition
  • Challenge Domains: Web Security, Cryptography, Digital Forensics, OSINT, Reverse Engineering, and Miscellaneous
  • Number of Challenges: To be announced through the official competition platform.
  • Competition Duration: The confirmed date, start time, end time, and total duration will be communicated through the official event listing or organizer announcements.

How It Works

  • Register: Complete your individual registration through Unstop.
  • Access the Platform: Follow the instructions provided by the organizers.
  • Solve Challenges: Investigate and solve problems across the available cybersecurity domains.
  • Capture the Flags: Find hidden flags and submit them through the designated platform.
  • Earn Points: Gain points for correctly solving challenges according to their assigned values.
  • Climb the Leaderboard: Compete individually against other participants.
  • Final Results: Rankings will be determined according to the official scoring and tie-breaking rules.

All challenges must be solved independently. Collaboration on solutions and sharing flags with other competitors during the competition are prohibited.

Rules and Regulations

  • Individual Participation: Every participant must compete independently. Team participation and joint submissions are prohibited.
  • Fair Play: Sharing flags, complete solutions, or restricted hints with other competitors during the event is not allowed.
  • Authorized Scope: Participants may test only the challenges and systems explicitly included within the competition scope.
  • No Infrastructure Attacks: Attacking the CTF platform, organizer infrastructure, or other participants' systems is strictly prohibited.
  • No Service Disruption: Denial-of-service attacks, excessive requests, or any activity intended to disrupt the competition are forbidden.
  • No Unauthorized Access: Accessing other participants' accounts, submissions, private data, or restricted resources is prohibited.
  • No Score Manipulation: Exploiting platform vulnerabilities to manipulate scores or obtain unauthorized points may result in disqualification.
  • Responsible Tool Usage: Tools and scripts may be used for legitimate challenge-solving purposes, provided they remain within the authorized scope and do not disrupt services.
  • No Plagiarism: Submitting another participant's work as your own is prohibited.
  • Report Technical Issues: Suspected vulnerabilities in the competition infrastructure must be reported privately to the organizers.
  • Account Responsibility: Participants must use their own registered accounts and are responsible for securing their credentials.
  • Professional Conduct: All participants must behave respectfully toward the organizers and fellow competitors.
  • Disqualification: Cheating, unauthorized attacks, rule violations, or attempts to gain an unfair advantage may result in disqualification.
  • Organizer Authority: The organizing team reserves the right to investigate violations, verify submissions, resolve disputes, and make final decisions regarding the results.
  • Schedule Updates: Any changes to the competition schedule, format, or instructions will be communicated through official channels.

Scoring and Leaderboard

  • Points will be awarded for correctly solving challenges and submitting valid flags.
  • Challenge scores may vary according to difficulty.
  • Rankings will be based on individual performance.
  • In case of a tie, the official tie-breaking criteria communicated by the organizers will apply.
  • Final results will be subject to score verification and compliance with the competition rules.

Get Ready for the Hunt

  • Every flag tells a story. Every challenge hides a clue. Every solution brings you one step closer to the truth.
  • The Last Daemon is about thinking differently, investigating carefully, and proving what you can accomplish on your own.
  • One participant. One mission. One ultimate hunt.

Are you ready to face The Last Daemon?

Organized by Beunwrapd — Empowering the next generation of cybersecurity talent.
